primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Pathogenic variants in desmosomal genes such as PKP2 impair intercellular mechanical adhesion among cardiomyocytes. Myocyte detachment and death, especially under mechanical stress, are followed by fibrofatty replacement that creates a substrate for ventricular arrhythmias.
vignette: A 26-year-old competitive cyclist is evaluated after exertional palpitations and syncope. His father died suddenly at age 34. Electrocardiography shows T-wave inversions in the right precordial leads, and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging shows right ventricular dilation with regional wall-motion abnormalities and fibrofatty myocardial replacement. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic PKP2 variant.
lead: Which cellular function is most directly impaired by this patient's pathogenic variant?
correct: Desmosome-mediated mechanical adhesion between adjacent cardiac myocytes
distractors: Sarcomere-mediated force generation by thick and thin filaments
Fast inward sodium current during phase 0 depolarization
Ryanodine receptor–mediated calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
Dystrophin-mediated linkage of the cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix
distractor_notes: Sarcomeric protein variants such as MYH7 and MYBPC3 are major causes of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; PKP2 instead encodes a desmosomal protein.
Reduced cardiac sodium current is a major mechanism in Brugada syndrome; it is not the direct cellular defect produced by a PKP2 variant.
RYR2 dysfunction disrupts intracellular calcium handling and is a major mechanism of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia; PKP2 does not encode a ryanodine receptor.
Dystrophin links the muscle-cell cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix and DMD variants can cause dilated cardiomyopathy; PKP2 is a desmosomal gene.
key_expl: The phenotype is consistent with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy. PKP2 encodes plakophilin-2, a component of cardiac desmosomes. Desmosomes mechanically couple adjacent cardiomyocytes. Pathogenic PKP2 variants impair desmosomal structure and function, allowing cardiomyocytes to detach and die under mechanical stress; the damaged myocardium is progressively replaced by fat and scar tissue, promoting ventricular arrhythmias.
objective: Relate a pathogenic PKP2 variant in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy to defective desmosome-mediated cardiomyocyte adhesion and subsequent fibrofatty myocardial replacement.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes ARVC as a myocardial disorder associated with arrhythmia and sudden death, especially during strenuous exercise, and explains that desmosomal gene variants impair desmosomes so cardiomyocytes detach and die, with damaged right ventricular myocardium replaced by fat and scar tissue. PKP2 is the most commonly implicated desmosomal gene.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: PKP2 gene
sources.locator: Normal Function; Health Conditions Related to Genetic Changes — Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
sources.support: MedlinePlus states that plakophilin-2 is a desmosomal protein in myocardium; desmosomes attach cells to one another and provide mechanical strength. PKP2 variants impair desmosomal formation/function and are associated with ARVC, cardiomyocyte loss, and fibrofatty replacement.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy
sources.support: NCBI describes progressive fibrofatty replacement, exercise-associated ventricular tachycardia, right-precordial T-wave inversion, cardiac magnetic resonance assessment, and the predominance of desmosomal genes including PKP2 in ARVC.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: Nonsyndromic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
sources.support: MedlinePlus identifies MYH7 and MYBPC3 as common genetic causes of nonsyndromic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and explains that many causative proteins are components of sarcomeres, the basic units of cardiac muscle contraction.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf
sources.title: Brugada Syndrome
sources.locator: Continuing Education Activity; History and Physical
sources.support: NCBI describes Brugada syndrome as commonly associated with SCN5A variants that impair cardiac sodium current, producing conduction abnormalities and ventricular arrhythmia risk.

sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.title: RYR2 gene
sources.locator: Normal Function; Health Conditions Related to Genetic Changes — Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
sources.support: MedlinePlus states that RYR2 forms a sarcoplasmic-reticulum calcium-release channel in cardiomyocytes and that pathogenic RYR2 variants are a major cause of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.

sources.title: DMD gene
sources.locator: Normal Function; Health Conditions Related to Genetic Changes — X-linked dilated cardiomyopathy
sources.support: MedlinePlus states that dystrophin anchors the muscle-cell cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix and that DMD variants can preferentially impair cardiac dystrophin and cause X-linked dilated cardiomyopathy.
